issues.description: Regex name HAS_TIME is slightly misleading since it's a heuristic pre-filter, not a definitive check
issues.detail: The name suggests definitive detection, but `/\dm?s/i` is a fast-path heuristic that can match non-time substrings like `1source` in identifiers/strings/urls. A name like `MAYBE_HAS_TIME` or a brief comment noting it's an optimization pre-filter would prevent future readers from assuming it's authoritative.

issues.description: No test added to verify the fast-path doesn't skip any legitimate time values
issues.detail: Since this changes the code path for every declaration, a regression test confirming edge cases (e.g., `.5s`, `5e2ms`, uppercase `5S`, `5MS`, calc expressions) still get linted would lock in the optimization. The `/i` flag handles case but a unit test would prevent future regressions if the regex is tweaked.

issues.description: Consider whether other similar rules would benefit from the same pattern
issues.detail: Issue #6869 likely covers multiple slow rules. If this is part of a broader perf effort, a shared utility for cheap unit pre-checks could avoid duplicating this pattern across rules. Not blocking for this PR but worth noting in the changeset or follow-up.

review.summary: Small, well-targeted performance fix: adds a cheap regex pre-check to skip the expensive `valueParser` call for declarations that can't contain a time value. The regex `/\dm?s/i` correctly covers all valid CSS time values (which must be `<digit...>s` or `<digit...>ms`), and false positives only trigger the existing slower path so there's no correctness risk. Main suggestions are cosmetic: clearer naming to signal it's a heuristic, and a small test guarding the fast-path against future edits. Safe to merge.
